json_document_profile.canonical_rule: Recursively sort object keys by Unicode code point; preserve array order; compact separators; UTF-8; ensure_ascii=false; finite numbers only; append exactly one LF.

selection_rule: Every tracked path in the exact base tree appears once in Git path order. Candidate files are absent from rows and listed separately. No working-tree file is used to define a predecessor row.

inventory.projection_rule: Canonical JSON plus LF of [[row[field] for field in row_schema] for row in rows] in exact row order.

candidate_additions.rule: Only these four paths may exist as untracked, unstaged candidate additions during drafting. They are not predecessor rows and no existing tracked path may change.

historical_byte_semantics.historical_objects: A historical predecessor lock governs the blob named by its historical Git object at its historical commit; accepted later changes do not rewrite that blob.
historical_byte_semantics.current_paths: Every current path is governed by the exact base-tree row in this manifest and by applicable accepted current authority; no current path is falsely required to equal a superseded historical blob.
historical_byte_semantics.stage_owned_declarations: D1 and D2 declaration modules, fixtures, and tests remain locked to their accepted integration objects and are not prospectively changed.
historical_byte_semantics.implementation_rule: A later compatibility implementation must reconstruct old blobs from Git, use current accepted identities for superseded paths, preserve unchanged historical rows in the working tree, and never rewrite a historical manifest.

projection_reconstruction.route_a: git ls-tree -rz --full-tree <base_head>, then git cat-file blob <object> for each row.
projection_reconstruction.route_b: git archive --format=tar <base_head>, read every regular or symbolic-link member in memory, normalize modes to 100644/100755/120000, and independently recompute paths, byte counts, and raw SHA-256 values.
projection_reconstruction.required_agreement: Both routes must yield exactly 269 paths in the same Git order and identical mode, payload length, and raw SHA-256 for every row. Route A additionally supplies Git object IDs.

enforcement: The exact base commit and tree must match before use.
Every row must reconstruct by both independent Git-object routes.
The tracked worktree and index must remain unchanged during authority drafting.
Exactly the four candidate additions may be untracked; staging, commit, push, merge, tag, or pull request is forbidden.
Any missing, extra, duplicate, reordered, mode-changed, object-changed, byte-changed, or hash-changed predecessor row fails closed.
nonclaims: This manifest changes no predecessor byte or Git object.
It authorizes no immediate test or production edit.
It authorizes no framework import, test execution, dependency installation, model state, scientific execution, Gate, result, manuscript, rendering, PDF, or publication operation.
